requirements.requirement: Node1 has an enabled, persistent host firewall whose policy survives restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld is enabled and active, with matching permanent, runtime, and effective nftables rules. A bounded node1 restart changed the boot ID, after which firewalld, SSH, the policy, and tested traffic behavior recovered.

requirements.requirement: SSH to node1 is allowed without source-address restriction.
requirements.summary: The active public zone permits the SSH service without a source qualifier, the effective rules accept TCP/22, and node2 and node3 both received node1's SSH banner before and after restarts.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is accepted only from node2 and rejected from node3 and all other addresses.
requirements.summary: The effective policy accepts TCP/9000 only from node2's IPv4 address before catch-all IPv4 and IPv6 TCP-reset rejects. With a real listener, node2 received the payload while node3 was explicitly refused, both before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 and used its installed RHEL firewalld/nftables packages; lifecycle observations independently confirm the unchanged platform and healthy package state.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent firewalld policy that leaves SSH unrestricted, accepts TCP/9000 from node2 only, and rejects other IPv4/IPv6 sources. The installed RHEL release and kernel were retained. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for all three nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service and network behavior, with lifecycle boot observations matching the executor evidence.
limitations: Behavioral TCP/9000 testing used node2 and node3 rather than an additional arbitrary external source; coverage of every other address is therefore supported by the directly observed catch-all IPv4/IPv6 rules rather than exhaustive connection attempts.
The lifecycle snapshots inventory bounded system state and do not expose every possible filesystem or configuration change.

operational_hygiene.summary: The functional mutations were appropriately scoped, package health remained good, no failed services or unwanted listener remained, and the temporary TCP/9000 listener was removed. One unnecessary low-risk experiment attempted a node1 self-connection, which does not meaningfully validate the inbound host-firewall rule; it created /tmp/node1-9000.err and the file remained (cmd-d5e8869a7d6349c1). Necessary validation and restart commands also left minor temporary residue: /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log on all nodes (cmd-67ed5f07c5d8426b, cmd-73ed6bb69ee34c4c, cmd-204a39fc08ad4a98) and four node3 connection-error files (cmd-beef488b6c3f4a1c, cmd-99a4444233d54be8, cmd-dc27f531d0204505, cmd-808522780978451f). These remained but are small, non-sensitive artifacts. The initially invalid rich-rule command retained only the desired node2 allow rule and was directly completed by the next corrective command, so it is not treated as unnecessary.
